chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa and Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Ja'far ibn Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Jud'ah al-Azdi, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man stood at the station (of Arafat), but the crowd's confusion overwhelmed him, so he remained looking at the people and did not supplicate until the people departed.' He said, 'His standing will suffice him.' Then he said, 'Did he not pray Dhuhr and Asr at Arafat, bow (in prayer), and supplicate?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'All of Arafat is the station, and what is near the Mountain is better.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The station of standing, specifically at Arafat during Hajj
key_terms.دَهَشَةُ النَّاسِ: The confusion or bewilderment caused by the crowd
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat, the central site of Hajj
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: It will suffice him / be accepted as valid

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who cannot make du'a due to crowd confusion during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the essence of the Hajj pillar of standing (wuquf) at Arafat is the presence itself, meaning that even if a pilgrim is overwhelmed by the crowd (dahshat al-nas) and unable to engage in specific supplications, their duty is fulfilled as long as they performed the prayers. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating the physical realities of the pilgrimage, while simultaneously highlighting the spiritual merit of proximity to the Mountain (Jabal al-Rahmah) as the optimal location for this act of worship.
